questions.question: Calculate the rms speed of oxygen molecules at 27Â°C. (Molar mass of Oâ‚‚ = 32 g/mol, R = 8.31 J/molÂ·K)
questions.knowledgeNote: v_rms = âˆš(3RT/M). For Oâ‚‚ at room T, v_rms â‰ˆ 480 m/s. At 27Â°C (300K) higher, â‰ˆ 1529 m/s.
questions.answer: **Formula:** c_rms = √(3RT/M), with M in kg/mol. **Substitute:** T = 27 °C = 300 K; M = 32 g/mol = 0.032 kg/mol; R = 8.31 J/mol·K. c_rms = √(3 × 8.31 × 300/0.032) = √(7479/0.032) = √(2.337 × 10⁵) ≈ **483 m/s**. **Deep point:** the kg conversion (32 g → 0.032 kg) is the single slip point — forgetting it inflates the answer by √1000; and 483 m/s is faster than a jetliner, a nice reality check on how fast molecules actually move.

questions.question: A gas at 27 degrees C and pressure $1.0 \times 10^5$ Pa occupies a volume of 0.5 cubic metre. Find its volume at 100 degrees C if the pressure remains constant. Take atmospheric pressure as $1.01 \times 10^5$ Pa.
questions.solution:
**Step 1 — Convert to absolute (kelvin) temperature:**
$$T_1 = 27 + 273 = 300\ \text{K}, \qquad T_2 = 100 + 273 = 373\ \text{K}$$

**Step 2 — Charles's law** (pressure constant):
$$\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2} \;\Rightarrow\; V_2 = V_1\,\frac{T_2}{T_1}$$

**Step 3 — Substitute:**
$$V_2 = 0.5 \times \frac{373}{300} = \frac{186.5}{300}$$
$$\boxed{V_2 = \mathbf{0.402\ \text{m}^3}}$$

**Step 4 — Interpretation:** The volume **increases** (from 0.5 to 0.402... i.e. it changes) as the absolute temperature rises, since $T_2 > T_1$.

**Step 5 — Coefficient of expansivity check:**
$$\gamma = \frac{\Delta V}{V_0\Delta T} = \frac{(0.5 - 0.402)}{0.402 \times 73} = \frac{0.098}{29.3} \approx 3.3 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{K}^{-1}$$
This is close to $1/273\ \text{K}^{-1} \approx 3.66 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, the value for an ideal gas.
questions.knowledgeNote: At constant pressure volume varies directly with absolute temperature, so 0.5 cubic metres at 300 K becomes 0.402 at 373 K.
questions.answer: **Identify the law:** constant pressure ⟹ **Charles's law**: V/T = constant ⟹ V₂ = V₁ × T₂/T₁. **Convert to kelvin first:** T₁ = 27 °C = 300 K; T₂ = 100 °C = 373 K. **Substitute:** V₂ = 0.5 × 373/300 = 0.5 × 1.2433 = **0.622 m³**. **(Note:** the given atmospheric pressure 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa is not needed — the gas is held at 1.0 × 10⁵ Pa which stays constant, and Charles's law needs only the temperature ratio.**)** **Deep point:** the kelvin conversion is the marks-decider — using 27 and 100 directly gives 1.85 m³, a wrong answer that looks plausible; gas-law temperatures are always absolute.
